standard-dialogue.npc: Is there something I can help ye with?

options.text: I would like to join your crew.

steps.player: I would like to join your crew.

steps.npc: Of course you would!

steps.text: If the player has something equipped in the helmet slot:

steps.npc: However, I don't let anyone on the team if they are wearing a hat or a helmet.
You can go and store it in the deposit box next to Jimmy's stall.

steps.player: Why not?

steps.npc: Well, in order to tell my crew from San Fan's I will need to give you a hat like mine.
If you are wearing a hat it might get lost when I give you my crew's hat.
You wouldn't want that would you?

steps.player: No, that sounds very reasonable in fact.

steps.text: If the player has items in their inventory:

steps.npc: Well, I'll be glad to have you aboard, but you will need to go and store all of your gear first.

steps.player: What do you mean?

steps.npc: Well, you will need all of your inventory space for the ingredients, and all of the other things I'll need you to haul about.
There is a bank deposit box next to Jimmy's stall if you need it. Come and see me when you have a fully empty inventory.

steps.text: If Fancy Dan's team has more players than San Fan's team:

steps.npc: Sadly for you however, I have more than enough people on my crew.

steps.player: Oh, all right.

steps.text: If the player has a cat following them:

steps.npc: Is that...thing yours?

steps.player: You mean my cat?

steps.npc: Yes, I mean your cat! I HATE cats! Get it out of here!
Filthy things, no better than the rats that they catch.

steps.text: If the player has a different follower out:
If the player does not have anything equipped in the helmet slot and no items in their inventory:

steps.npc: Arr, well we'll get you sorted out with a team hat right away.
Go wait in the waiting room, I'll call you when we are ready to begin.

steps.text: The player is teleported into the Trouble Brewing waiting room.

options.text: Who are you, and what is this place?

steps.player: Who are you, and what is this place?

steps.npc: Arrharrharr!
Do you not recognise me? I am the famous dandy pirate 'Fancy' Dan!

steps.player: Yes, of course, any pirate knows who you are.

steps.npc: But of course.
As for what this place is, it is my glorious still, producing the best quality 'rum' this side of Braindeath Island.
Oh, and the run-down swill-producing ditch that San Fan over there calls a still.

steps.player: So with two stills you have plenty of 'rum' right?

steps.npc: Well we would do, if that hatchet-faced harridan wouldn't keep trying to torch the place!

steps.player: I say!

steps.npc: A little while ago we had some real problems getting rum to the island, hence the two stills.
However, after a little misunderstanding involving San's still and a barrel of gunpowder our relationship seems to have become a little strained.
Apparently it is perfectly within the pirate code to burn each others stills, so long as nobody directly attacks the other person's crew, so rum production has taken a slight dip of late.

steps.player: Can I help out?

steps.npc: Yes, probably. I have a bunch of jobs that need doing, if you feel up to it.
What would you like to know about?

options.text: Brewing 'Rum'

steps.player: How do I help you brew 'Rum'?

steps.npc: Well the stills we have set up are based on the ones on Braindeath island... well roughly at any rate.
All you have to do is help put the ingredients into the hoppers and keep the boilers burning.
If you add enough ingredients to the hoppers then you have the ability to pick up a single bottle of rum when it brews.

So, if ye add 5 buckets of water to the hoppers, then ye get access to one bottle. If you add 3 bowls of coloured water you get access to one bottle, and if you add one of anything else you get access to one bottle.
This is cumulative, meaning that if you add (for example) 10 buckets of water, 3 sweetgrubs and 6 bowls of coloured water, then you have a chance to collect 7 bottles of rum for the team.
The boilers are easy as pie to sort out. You just put some logs in, light them with a tinderbox, and then keep putting logs in until they are good and hot.
Three logs should do it, but it's best to keep heaping them in just in case.
The ingredients are; Bitternuts, Scrapey Tree Bark, Sweetgrubs, Buckets of Water and some Coloured Water.

options.text: Where can I get Bitternuts?

steps.player: Where can I get Bitternuts?

steps.npc: There are plenty of Bitternut trees inside this walled off area. The problem is that the trees are too tricky for a human to climb.
You will need to catch a monkey and send it up the tree to get the nut for you.

steps.player: Send it up the tree? How does that work?

steps.npc: Well, if you were a monkey, and some random person grabbed you, dumped some dye in your fur and shoved you up a tree, you would hurl the closest heavy object at them too.

steps.player: Wait a second, dye?

steps.npc: Yes, you'll need to get a bowl of coloured water and pour it on the monkey. Otherwise you won't be able to tell which team the monkey belongs too.

steps.player: That makes sense...I think...

steps.npc: Anything else?

options.text: Can I ask about something else?

steps.player: Can I ask about something else?

steps.npc: Ok, what else?

steps.player: So...how would I go about sabotaging the enemy still?

Where can I get Scrapey Tree Bark?

steps.player: Where can I get Scrapey tree bark...and why do I get the feeling I won't like the answer?

steps.npc: Inside this walled area there are a few Scrapey trees. They are the big, ill looking ones, you can't miss them.
Basically, you cut them down and then carve the bark off with a knife.
It's pretty simple, except the sap tends so make people feel kind off ill if they get any on themselves.

steps.player: How ill?

steps.npc: Don't worry, we aren't talking deadly ill or anything.
It's more like you'll feel quite dizzy and weak for a bit.

steps.player: Joy...

steps.npc: Anything else?

Where can I get Sweetgrubs?

steps.player: Sweetgrubs? What are they?

steps.npc: Well, lacking any sluglings in the area, we add these little grubs called Sweetgrubs. If you ignore the gag- inducing aftertaste, they are quite sweet.

steps.player: How... how can you drink this stuff?

steps.npc: Quite easily!
Pirates are renowned as being tough for a reason.

steps.player: So where do I get these grubs from anyway?

steps.npc: Well, there are a few sweetgrub mounds inside there. We have a handful of rat meat that you can use on the mounds to draw the grubs to the surface.
Mind your fingers though, they are voracious little things.

steps.player: And here was me thinking that nothing could be more disgusting than Braindeath 'Rum'.

steps.speaker: Captian Braindeath
steps.text: Arr, that's where ye'd be wrong [lad/lass], 'cos new, improved Braindeath 'Rum' Classic is now 200% more disgustin' than any leadin' competitor!

steps.speaker: Captian Braindeath
steps.text: Legal disclaimer; the dangerous amount of disgustin' in new Braindeath 'Rum' Classic be too much for pregnant women, donkeys and anyone with more than seven letters in their last name.

steps.player: What sort of coloured water are we talking about here?

steps.npc: Well, the other still has an area of waste ground with a flower growing on it. If you go and grab one of the flowers and jam it in the kettle, the water will boil out the colour.
We use the colour to keep our rum easily identifiable.

steps.player: So I just empty the kettle into the hopper, right?

steps.npc: No, no, you'll need to take an empty bowl and fill it from the kettle.
That way you can use the stuff on a monkey if you need to.

Repairing the Still

steps.player: How do I repair the still?

steps.npc: Well, assuming those scurvy dogs have managed to set any of it on fire, then you'll need to tip a bucket of water on it before you can repair it.
Then, it all comes down to what part of it was damaged.

options.text: How do I repair Hoppers?

steps.player: How can I repair hoppers?

steps.npc: Well, assuming that they are not on fire, all you need to do is use the heavy lumber patches. They are big enough to cover most holes.

steps.player: Will I need a hammer?

steps.npc: No, just shove it into place and whack it until it lines up.
Anything else?

steps.npc: Well, if you use a pipe section on the damaged part you should be able to replace it easily.

steps.player: Will I need a hammer?

steps.npc: No, likely you'll just need to whack the old one out and slot the new one in with your hands.

steps.player: How do I repair bridges?

steps.npc: Well, we have these handy bridge sections you can use to repair the bridges.
The main problem is, while a still will keep working if a bit of it is only damaged, the bridges are completely out of commission if they are even slightly damaged.

steps.player: Is that going to be a problem? I mean, I can jump across I think.

steps.npc: Don't try that! Our lawyers tell us we aren't covered for injuries sustained while jumping over burned bridges.
Seriously, just keep off the bridges until they are fixed.
Anything else?

jump-8c836d61e6bfb7b2.player: And here was me thinking that nothing could be more disgusting than Braindeath 'Rum'.

jump-8c836d61e6bfb7b2.speaker: Captian Braindeath
jump-8c836d61e6bfb7b2.text: Arr, that's where ye'd be wrong [lad/lass], 'cos new, improved Braindeath 'Rum' Classic is now 200% more disgustin' than any leadin' competitor!

jump-8c836d61e6bfb7b2.speaker: Captian Braindeath
jump-8c836d61e6bfb7b2.text: Legal disclaimer; the dangerous amount of disgustin' in new Braindeath 'Rum' Classic be too much for pregnant women, donkeys and anyone with more than seven letters in their last name.

jump-e255ba41666a4f6f.npc: There are plenty of Bitternut trees inside this walled off area. The problem is that the trees are too tricky for a human to climb.
You will need to catch a monkey and send it up the tree to get the nut for you.

jump-e255ba41666a4f6f.player: Send it up the tree? How does that work?

jump-e255ba41666a4f6f.npc: Well, if you were a monkey, and some random person grabbed you, dumped some dye in your fur and shoved you up a tree, you would hurl the closest heavy object at them too.
Yes, you'll need to get a bowl of coloured water and pour it on the monkey. Otherwise you won't be able to tell which team the monkey belongs too.
